criteria.requirement: A node that loses one path to the LUN under load keeps working on the other; when the lost path returns it is reinstated and carries the I/O when the path that survived is lost in turn. No operation fails on any node, no node is fenced or stops, no lock is granted twice, and every acknowledged file is intact.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_failover.sh (host-coordinated; F1 and F2 of docs/mpath-verification.md): every node runs tests/mpath/pathload.py (fsynced checksummed files, shared-directory churn, a mkdir mutual-exclusion witness); the last node's path on storage network a is taken down at the hypervisor (scripts/san_net.sh link) for 60 s, restored, awaited usable (bound 60 s), then its path on network b is taken down for 60 s and restored. PASS only when, per fault, every node's longest gap between completed operations is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound, zero operations errored, the kept path's write counter advanced and the removed path's did not in the second half of the window; and overall zero double grants, every acknowledged file read back with its sha256 from another node, no membership beacon below N, no shutdown/BUG/oops/hung task, 2 usable NIC-bound paths on every node at start and end, and the target's reservation keys identical at start and end.

criteria.why: Multipath exists for the moment a path is lost. A board that passes on two healthy paths says nothing about that moment, and a site told mpath works will pull a cable on day one.

criteria.requirement: When a whole storage network is lost, every node fails over to the other together and keeps working; when it returns every node reinstates it, and the cluster survives losing the other network in turn. No operation fails, no node is fenced or stops, no lock is granted twice, and every acknowledged file is intact.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_fabric.sh (host-coordinated; F3 of docs/mpath-verification.md): under tests/mpath/pathload.py on every node, every node's path on storage network a is taken down at once for 60 s, restored and awaited usable on every node (bound 60 s), then the same for network b. PASS only when, per loss, every node's longest stall is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound, zero operations errored, and on every node the kept path's write counter advanced and the lost path's did not; and overall zero double grants, every acknowledged file read back by sha256 from another node, no shutdown/withdrawal/death/BUG in any node's kernel journal, 2 usable NIC-bound paths everywhere at start and end, and the target's reservation keys unchanged.

criteria.why: The common production path failure is not one cable: a switch or a fabric dies and every node fails over at the same moment, each stalled while the locks it needs are held by peers that are stalled too.

criteria.requirement: A path that goes down and comes back repeatedly, faster than multipathd settles it, costs no operation, no node and no lock.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_flap.sh (host-coordinated; F4 of docs/mpath-verification.md): under tests/mpath/pathload.py on every node, the last node's path on network a is taken down and brought back 10 times, 4 s each state; then 30 s of load on the settled paths. PASS only when across the flapping window and after it every node's longest stall is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound and zero operations errored, the victim is back on 2 usable paths within 60 s, zero double grants, every acknowledged file read back by sha256 from another node, no shutdown/withdrawal/death/BUG in any kernel journal, and the target's reservation keys unchanged.

criteria.why: A failing cable or port flaps before it dies; failovers and reinstatements then overlap, which a single clean cut never exercises.

criteria.requirement: A node can join the cluster while one of its paths is down, uses that path once it returns, can leave while a different path is down, and leaves no reservation registration behind on a path that was down when it left.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_mount_degraded.sh (host-coordinated; F8 of docs/mpath-verification.md): the other nodes run tests/mpath/pathload.py throughout. The last node unmounts on two paths; its path on network a is taken down at the hypervisor and, once multipathd has failed it, the node mounts (bound 60 s) and runs the load; path a is restored and reinstated (bound 60 s) and the target must then hold the node's key on both paths; path b is taken down for 40 s and the node's I/O must continue on path a; with b still down the node unmounts; b is restored and the target must hold no registration of the node; the node mounts again. PASS only when every mount and unmount returned 0, the stall at the late fault is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound with zero errors and the kept path carrying the writes, zero double grants, every acknowledged file read back by sha256 from another node, no shutdown/withdrawal/death/BUG in any kernel log, and the registration counts are 2(N-1), 2N, 2(N-1), 2N at the four checkpoints.

criteria.why: A fence is a reservation command and a replay is I/O; both must work for a node that has itself lost a path, and the fence must clear the dead node's key from both of its paths.

criteria.requirement: A node fenced while one of its paths was down is refused on both paths when that path returns: its key does not come back, it stops by itself instead of hanging, nothing it writes afterwards is acknowledged, and it can rejoin as a new incarnation.

PASS only when for 40 s after the thaw the target held exactly the others' registrations at every sample, the victim's kernel log shows its authority closed or the filesystem shut down, a probe write on it failed and returned, its load ended when told, no fsynced write it started after being frozen was acknowledged, it unmounted and mounted again (rc 0, 0) and ran the load without error, the others' longest stall is under 120 s with zero errors, zero double grants, and every acknowledged file reads back by sha256 from another node.

criteria.why: Multipath cannot help a node with no path left; what must hold is that it stops rather than hangs holding locks, and that its queued writes are refused when the paths come back.

criteria.requirement: A node that shuts its filesystem down and leaves with its reservation key already gone is recovered by the others, whether they are on two paths or one, and can join again.
criteria.detector: tests/mpath/path_peer_withdrawn.sh (host-coordinated; F10): under tests/mpath/pathload.py on every node, the last node stops its load, shuts its filesystem down (XFS_IOC_GOINGDOWN, no log flush) and unmounts. PASS only when its registrations left the target within 60 s, a survivor reported its recovery complete within 120 s, every survivor's load kept completing with zero errors and no stall over 120 s, and the node mounted again and ran the load; then the same again with storage network a down on every survivor (each survivor's remaining path carrying the writes), network a restored, every node registered on both paths within 30 s, every acknowledged file read back by sha256 from another node, zero double grants, and no survivor shut down or withdrew.

PASS only when the victim's kernel log shows at least one resent COMPARE AND WRITE that met its own write (P-CAW-ANSWER-LOST-LANDED), per fault every node's longest stall is under tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound with zero errors and the kept path carrying the writes, zero double grants, every acknowledged file reads back by sha256 from another node, no shutdown/withdrawal/death/BUG, and the target's reservation keys are unchanged.

criteria.requirement: After a dirty node death on the shared LUN and the survivor's foreign replay of the dead slice, the platter is structurally intact: the offline checker cold on the survivor's LUN reports no violation, the chunk/free-space aliasing pass is OK, the superblock icount/ifree equal the inobt sums, and every file the victim had fsync-acknowledged before its death has its inode allocated in the cold inobt. The orderly audit (chk_clean) cannot speak for this path: unmount drains, commits and writes the counters.
criteria.detector: tests/death/crash_audit.sh (host-coordinated, terminal): tests/tcp_death_replay.sh plain arm (victim virsh-destroyed 6 s into an fsynced stream; survivor's heartbeat expiry, fence, sealed manifest, foreign replay, recovery complete, every acknowledged file md5-verified), then the survivor records the replayed inode numbers, unmounts as the last member, and chk_mxfs -v runs cold on it; RESULT PASS only when the oracle passed with acked >= 1 AND rc 0 / zero error lines / aliasing OK / icount==inobt sum / ifree==inobt free sum / every replayed inode allocated. Leaves the fleet unmounted (the next prep re-forms it).
